title: Automakers warn Trump's 50% tariffs would be 'devastating'
summary: Industry stakeholders warned that doubling U.S. tariffs on Canadian-made vehicles, and potentially extending them to auto parts, would have a severe impact on both the Canadian and U.S. automotive sectors. The warning comes as the Trump administration considers escalating tariffs from 25% to 50% on vehicles imported from Canada.

title: At Apple CEO's Farewell, Tributes and an Unusually Personal Tim Cook
summary: At a farewell event marking Tim Cook's departure as Apple CEO, colleagues and industry figures paid tribute to his tenure, and Cook offered an unusually personal account of his time leading the company. The event underscores Apple's transition away from Cook, who has led the company since 2011.

title: Cursor Officially Enters Its Musk Era
summary: AI coding startup Cursor has formally become part of Elon Musk's business orbit, aligning with SpaceX as the company undergoes a transformation. The Information reports on how Cursor's direction and priorities are shifting as a result of the new relationship.

title: FCC okays 30-day AST SpaceMobile D2D smartphone tests
summary: The FCC granted AST SpaceMobile a 30-day special temporary authority to test satellite-to-smartphone direct-to-device connectivity using up to 100 off-the-shelf handsets in the 800MHz band, with testing permitted through September 12 near Midland, Texas, and Lanham, Maryland. The authorization is limited to non-commercial testing under AST's existing agreement with T-Mobile.

title: Ericsson: AI could make edge computing viable for telecoms
summary: Ericsson said AI-driven demand for low-latency processing is making edge computing commercially viable for telecom operators, as networks increasingly place compute power closer to where data is generated, such as at base stations. The company cites measurable gains including spectrum efficiency, energy savings, and coverage improvements from embedding AI directly into radio access networks.

title: AI boom turning network buildouts into policy problem
summary: Broadband providers say the simultaneous buildout of AI data center infrastructure by hyperscalers is straining supply chains and worsening permitting delays for their own network expansion. Industry executives cite rising costs, particularly for memory components, and warn policymakers may need to reconsider timelines for federal broadband programs as a result.

title: Filling In the Gaps in Nvidia's $500 Billion Financing Pitch
summary: Nvidia has lined up Blackstone, Apollo, Goldman Sachs and other financial firms to potentially finance $500 billion of AI infrastructure purchases, but the arrangement remains in early development with only memorandums of understanding signed so far. The Information examines how the financing could work, drawing on a $35 billion Broadcom-backed deal for Google TPUs as the closest analogue, with lenders expected to weigh chip residual value and Nvidia's proposed 25% loss-coverage guarantee.

title: Amazon Becomes Vital Sales Outlet For Independent Merchants
summary: Amazon has become the most important sales channel for a wide range of independent brands and merchants, as declining organic search traffic and rising advertising costs elsewhere push sellers toward the platform. The Information reports the shift is reinforcing Amazon's leverage over smaller retailers who increasingly depend on it for discovery and sales.

title: Thomson Reuters launches its own AI model to reduce reliance on big tech
summary: Thomson Reuters launched a proprietary large language model, dubbed "Thomson," marking an early test of whether a domain-specific AI model can compete with general-purpose offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI. The move reflects an effort by the company to reduce its dependence on outside AI providers.

title: Introducing the AI Model 'Harness'
summary: WSJ profiles the growing enterprise concept of an AI "model harness" -- the software layer that gives AI models memory, business context, and the ability to take actions -- as companies weigh whether to build custom harnesses in-house or rely on vendor-built ones. Moody's built its own harness-like tool called the Research Assistant, while Bristol-Myers Squibb adopted Anthropic's Claude as its standard harness to avoid rebuilding infrastructure tooling.

title: Private Equity Is Deploying an Army of AI Wonks to Embed in the Firms They Back
summary: Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman have formed a roughly 160-person team of AI experts with Anthropic to deploy across businesses, starting with their own portfolio companies, as part of a $1.5 billion joint venture that also includes Apollo, General Atlantic and Goldman Sachs as backers. The venture aims to embed AI engineers directly inside portfolio companies to redesign workflows rather than operate as a traditional consulting arrangement.

title: Alibaba to Bulk Up AI Investment Via $10.2 Billion Share Placement
summary: Alibaba priced an HK$80 billion ($10.2 billion) placement of 710 million new shares to investors outside the U.S. at HK$112.70 per share to fund its AI infrastructure buildout, including chips and model development. The placement, one of the largest primary follow-on share sales globally this year, came days after Alibaba reported a sharp profit decline tied to heavy AI spending, and shares fell on the news.

title: TikTok agrees $400M US privacy settlement
summary: TikTok and parent company ByteDance agreed to pay $400 million to settle a Justice Department lawsuit alleging the platform violated children's online privacy law by collecting data on users under 13 without parental consent. Under the settlement, TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and an additional $100 million once a prior consent decree tied to its Musical.ly predecessor is vacated.

title: MTN triggers $375M share scheme, reveals Iran plans
summary: South African telecom group MTN launched a ZAR6 billion ($375 million) share buyback after first-half service revenue grew 17.5% and profit rose over 21%, even as shareholder profit fell 25% due to impairments tied to its Iranian unit, Irancell. CEO Ralph Mupita reiterated the company's plans for its Iran business should U.S. sanctions be lifted, as MTN continues seeking to exit the market.

title: Nvidia in early talks with chip startup Rebellions
summary: Nvidia is in early discussions with South Korean AI chip designer Rebellions about a possible technical partnership, investment, or acquisition, according to Bloomberg. Rebellions, founded in 2020, has raised roughly $850 million and was most recently valued at about $2.3 billion; talks are described as preliminary and may not lead to a transaction.

title: DeepSeek takes aim at Anthropic with new model
summary: DeepSeek released an experimental multimodal model, V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, that it says approaches the performance of Anthropic's Opus 4.8 on agentic benchmarks, outperforming it on 3 of 11 tests including Agents Last Exam and ZeroBench. The model can process images alongside text and handle up to 600 images per request, though DeepSeek acknowledged it still trails Opus 4.8 on other benchmarks such as NL2Repo.

title: Canadian investors are dumping U.S. government debt for American corporate bonds
summary: Canadian investors are shifting portfolios away from U.S. government debt toward American corporate bonds, driven by concerns over U.S. fiscal policy and a surge in AI-related corporate borrowing, according to economists. The Logic reports the trend reflects broader unease about the sustainability of U.S. federal deficits.

title: Nvidia Discusses Perplexity Investment at $30 Billion-Plus Valuation
summary: Nvidia is discussing an investment in Perplexity as part of a funding round that would value the AI search startup at more than $30 billion, over 50% above its valuation a year ago. Perplexity's annualized revenue has grown to more than $750 million from under $250 million at the start of the year, helped by its Perplexity Computer AI agent product.

title: Political Backlash Against AI Data Centers Intensifies
summary: A March Gallup survey found 71% of Americans would oppose construction of a data center in their local area, compared with 53% who said the same of a nuclear plant. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, who previously championed the industry, signed an executive order this week imposing new restrictions on data-center construction, part of a broader wave of political pushback prompting tech companies to hold community listening sessions and fund local investments to shore up public support.

title: OpenAI's Q2 Sales Growth Trails Anthropic as Losses Widen
summary: OpenAI told investors its revenue grew 18% quarter-over-quarter to $6.7 billion in the second quarter, while its operating losses deepened, results that disappointed shareholders hoping for more progress narrowing the gap with Anthropic. Anthropic's revenue more than doubled to $11.6 billion in the same period, marking the first time its sales surpassed OpenAI's.

title: $3 Trillion in AI-Related Spending Sits Off Corporate Balance Sheets
summary: A Wall Street Journal analysis of securities-filing footnotes found nine major technology companies, including Alphabet, Meta and Oracle, have amassed roughly $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments mostly tied to AI infrastructure. Those obligations are growing faster than the companies' reported capital expenditures, which totaled about $600 billion over the past year, suggesting the true scale of AI-related financial exposure is larger than standard financial statements show.

title: Nvidia Commits $6 Billion to Build US Alternative to Chinese Open-Weight AI
summary: Nvidia struck a deal worth roughly $6 billion to license startup Poolside's technology and bring more than 100 of its employees onto Nvidia's Nemotron open-weight model project, alongside a separate $1 billion investment in Poolside at a $12 billion pre-money valuation. The move aims to build one of the world's most powerful open-weight AI models to compete with Chinese systems such as DeepSeek and Kimi K3, as well as US rivals OpenAI and Anthropic.

title: Nvidia AI Chip Prices to Rise About 17%, Server Makers Tell Customers
summary: Server makers have notified customers that prices for some of Nvidia's flagship AI server chip systems, including Grace Blackwell 300 and Vera Rubin 200 systems due for delivery next year, are set to rise by roughly 17%. The increase could add at least $5 billion to the cost of building a 1-gigawatt AI data center, according to people familiar with the notifications.

title: Anthropic Publishes AI-Native Software Development Lifecycle Playbook
summary: Anthropic released a playbook for redesigning the software development lifecycle around AI agents, arguing that approval gates and handoffs built for human-written code are now the bottleneck as agentic coding tools like Claude Code accelerate the build phase. The playbook groups recommendations into six stages, plan, design, build, test, deploy and maintain, each with guidance on adoption, governance and measuring impact.

title: Deloitte Publishes AI-Era Workforce Planning Blueprint
summary: Deloitte published a guide to modernizing workforce planning for the AI era, finding that 88% of leaders consider it extremely or very important to accelerate how people and skills are organized, but only 7% report making great progress. The guide sets out a three-stage blueprint, measure, plan and execute, along with a maturity model for sequencing AI-related workforce investments.

title: Intel Survey Finds Wide Gap in Enterprise Robotics Readiness
summary: An Intel survey of 800 senior business, IT, robotics and government leaders found that on average, deploying a robot is expected to beat the cost of hiring a human within three years, and six in ten leaders expect to operate a robot fleet within five years. While 67% expect to manage a mixed human-robot workforce by 2030, only 40% currently have a formal strategy in place for it.

title: Startup Founders Are Working Harder Than Ever to Keep Up With Their AI Agents
summary: As AI agents take on more complex tasks autonomously, startup founders report working longer hours to supervise, correct, and manage the output of these systems rather than working less. The trend marks a shift in startup work culture, with AI's expanding capabilities increasing rather than easing the operational burden on founders. The dynamic raises questions about the near-term productivity gains promised by agentic AI tools.

title: AI's Need for Content Has Put Rare-Book Dealers in a Bind
summary: Rising demand for training data to power large language models has fueled a boom in the rare and antiquarian book trade as AI companies and data brokers seek original text sources. Dealers report increased sales but are conflicted over whether historic, irreplaceable volumes are being consumed as raw material for AI training rather than preserved for their own value. The trend highlights growing tension between the AI industry's appetite for content and traditional book collecting and preservation.
